\section*{Chapter 3 --- Methodology}

\subsection*{Problem, Requirements and Scope}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \flag{The real recordings were
driven at \SI{0.28}{\metre\per\second}, not \SI{1.5}{}, so the real-robot
RPE is measured under an easier condition than the target assumes
(\reportref{sec:exp1-real}).} The proposal's localization requirement of
\SI{0.1}{\metre} under scheduled illumination changes is not carried: no
illumination experiment was run (\reportref{sec:deviations}).

\medskip

\subsection*{The Pipelines as Implemented: Navigation and relocalisation integration: the
\repo{vslam_navigation} package}
\noindent\textbf{2.}\quad \emph{table row:} Forward collision check \textbar{} off \textbar{} \flag{on} \textbar{} \flag{asymmetric; see below}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{3.}\quad \emph{table row:} Forward collision check \textbar{} off \textbar{} \flag{on} \textbar{} \flag{asymmetric; see below}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.}\quad \flag{The real rig
keeps it on, untested, because its prior map is the less trustworthy of the two
and no run yet exists to show which failure matters more there.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{5.}\quad The published
speed is also capped in the robot's own command units, which are not
metres per second and whose scale is known only at a single operating point
( \flag{the speed scale is provisional; \reportref{sec:real-platform}} ).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad Each run of the sweep writes a manifest beside its data recording the settings
it used, the full launch command, the git commit and the wall duration, and
\repo{script/aisle_sweep.py --analyse} reads them into a single table, so a
result cannot be attributed to the wrong configuration. \flag{An earlier revision of this chapter stated that the sweep had no scored
summary and that its run directories recorded the estimator configuration but
not the relocalisation parameters. That is no longer true and the statement is
withdrawn.} Its one carried conclusion --- that run-to-run spread over identical
settings is as wide as most differences between settings --- is used in
\reportref{sec:exp4-sim} to refuse comparisons.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulated sensor rig and platform}
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad \emph{table row:} \texttt{gyr\_n} \textbar{} 0.002 \textbar{} \flag{0.00030--0.00036} \textbar{} rad\,s$^{-1}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The configured gyroscope noise density is \num{2e-3} whereas the stationary
windows of the four recordings give \numrange{3.0e-4}{3.6e-4}, so the
configured value is five to seven times too large. The configured accelerometer
density of 0.02 sits inside the measured spread, but that spread is itself wide,
\numrange{0.015}{0.024} across four recordings of the same simulated sensor.
Both estimators therefore run on an inertial noise model that does not describe
this IMU closely. The bias random walks cannot be checked at all: the longest
stationary interval in any recording is \SI{2.16}{\second} and an
Allan-variance estimate needs minutes. This discrepancy is not incidental: by
the design decision of \reportref{sec:proprio-method} the EKF baseline is run on
these same configured values, so the comparison between the proprioceptive and
visual families is made at a shared handicap rather than at each family's best.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The accelerometer characterisation is not stable across recordings of the same
simulated sensor. The $x$ bias ranges from \SI{0.013}{} to
\SI{0.079}{\metre\per\second\squared} and the $x$ scale from 1.017 to 1.095
over the four recordings, while the gyroscope $z$ scale agrees to within
\num{0.0007} over the same four. Because the stationary window is between
\SI{1.14}{} and \SI{2.16}{\second} in every case, part of that spread is
estimator variance rather than a property of the sensor, and the accelerometer
terms should not be quoted as calibrated constants.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulation fidelity and its limits}
\noindent\textbf{10.}\quad \emph{table row:} Accelerometer, per axis (\si{\metre\per\second\squared}) \textbar{} \num{0.0566} \textbar{} \num{4.002e-3} \textbar{} \flag{\numrange{1.5e-2}{2.4e-2}} \textbar{} \num{2.00e-3}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{11.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{slip1}, \repo{slip2} \textbar{} 0 on all grounds \textbar{} \flag{an ODE feature;
  \repo{dartsim} does not implement it, so inert at any value}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{12.\ \flag{[Threat to validity]}}\quad This is a bias with a known direction. The EKF baseline of
\reportref{sec:results-proprio} is evaluated on a floor where the wheels effectively
cannot slip and with an encoder of unlimited resolution, which is dead
reckoning's best case. Both idealisations favour the proprioceptive estimators
over the visual ones, and neither has been relaxed. Any conclusion that a
wheel-plus-IMU filter matches or beats the visual pipelines should be read as
holding \emph{under these conditions}, not as a general result.
\repo{script/make_slippery_floor.py} generates ground models at a chosen
friction coefficient so that traction can be made an experimental factor, and
\repo{script/encoder_sim.py} imposes a realistic quantisation floor. Neither has
been used in any result reported here.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{13.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{gyr_w} \textbar{} \num{0.0001} \textbar{} \num{1.735e-6} \textbar{} \flag{\num{58}$\times$} \textbar{} gyroscope bias random walk

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.\ \flag{[Retired evidence for the inflated setting]}}\quad The inflated configuration is retained for every result in this report, on the
strength of an experiment that is no longer part of the reported campaign: in
September 2026 both estimators were re-run on configurations carrying the true
injected densities, and although accuracy improved wherever a run completed,
three of ten runs diverged outright where the inflated configuration diverged in
none. That evidence was recorded on recordings retired on 6 November 2026, so it
is reported here as the reason for a setting rather than as a result, and the
comparison has not been repeated on the current recordings.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Realistic logistics layouts}
\noindent\textbf{15.}\quad \flag{The generator reproduces the U world exactly but no longer
reproduces the I world: it would now emit eight dock-line items instead of
thirteen and two more clutter instances. The committed world file is the
recorded environment and is the source of these counts.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{16.\ \flag{[Visual verification]}}\quad The generator-side checks are complete, and the first Gazebo session on
6 October 2026 found and fixed one defect the checks could not see (a jack
setting its load down and then stopping on the neighbouring cell, because the
drop command carried one angle for both the parked load and the approach
heading). Three things remain to be confirmed by eye in the simulator rather
than by the checker: that the loads ride on the fork side of the jack, the
shading of the generated door, trailer and yard meshes, and the open/closed
state of each door. Until then the worlds are \status{implemented} in geometry
and \status{partial} in visual verification.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{17.\ \flag{[Provenance]}}\quad None of the six recordings carries a run manifest of its own: the world each
was recorded in is known from the manifests of the replays made on it, not
from the recording. Those manifests agree, and the object inventory each bag
reports is consistent with the layout they name, but a recording whose world
is attested only by later use is weaker evidence than one that records its own
world. A manifest should be written at record time, not at replay time.

\medskip

the hardware diagram (a single traction motor with a steering servo) and the

\subsection*{Planned Versus Implemented}
\noindent\textbf{27.}\quad \emph{table row:} Dynamic-object handling \textbar{} YOLO26 detection, masking the detector's boxes out of
  the estimator \textbar{} dropped. Experiment~1 found that physically simulated
  traffic neither broke tracking nor drove the global error, whose large
  failures are the loop closer's, and that its one dangerous case, a vehicle
  leading the robot, raised the per-second error two- to eightfold for four
  seconds and left under \SI{0.1}{\metre} in the accumulated error
  (\reportref{sec:results-validity}); the masking arm that would have consumed the
  detector was never run. \flag{The finding holds at the simulated traffic
  density, whose realism is assumed and not measured, and has no real-robot
  counterpart.} \textbar{} dropped

\section*{Chapter 4 --- Experiments and Results}

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four \repo{dataset_allsensor_realistic} recordings, two
layouts each recorded without and with warehouse traffic. Two families of
estimator are scored over the full common interval of each: the non-visual
ones --- wheel odometry, IMU dead reckoning, an EKF at the visual systems' own
inertial noise configuration and a measured-noise EKF as diagnostic --- and
the visual ones, VINS-Fusion once per recording and ORB-SLAM3 with a CPU or
GPU feature extractor and its loop closer active or disabled. Traffic is noted
as a condition, not tested as a factor. The latency and resource measurement
is taken from eighteen repeated runs on the two mapping recordings, three
repeats of each of six configurations, and those repeats are the only
within-configuration spread the campaign measures.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{2.}\quad \flag{Those two clean values are not themselves as low
as the stable runs', which span \SIrange{0.016}{0.037}{\metre}.} Which front-end condition produces them is not isolated here; the CPU runs of
the same recordings are scored below, where the same pattern recurs.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{3.}\quad \flag{One run per cell, and ORB-SLAM3's spread
  over identical repeats reaches \SI{0.277}{\metre} on these recordings ---
  wider than five of the eight gaps in (b) --- so no individual line is
  evidence. What the figure supports is the contrast between the panels: a
  shift every pair agrees on against one they do not.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.}\quad \flag{The low-feature seconds are \SIrange{8}{20}{\percent}
of each run and carry about that share of its error growth, so this is the
cause of VINS-Fusion's excursions and not of its ATE.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{5.}\quad \flag{One robust
relationship is left out of the claims because it has no mechanism: frames
with more extracted features carry fewer tracked map points, in all sixteen
runs, and the obvious explanation --- that feature-rich views are new scene
--- failed its test.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad \flag{One
  repeat on one recording: it establishes that the excursion belongs to the
  recording and not to the run, and no more.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad \flag{The hypothesis this project is
named for is therefore supported in one configuration, a vehicle leading the
robot, as a strong local effect on both estimators and a small accumulated
one, over four seconds of a 117-second recording; "movers degrade the
estimate" as a general statement is not what these recordings show.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.}\quad The jack had been in view, moving, for the nine seconds
  before the band --- \SIrange{6}{20}{\metre} away and small in the image ---
  with no effect; the cost begins when it is close enough to fill the view. \flag{One episode on one recording: it shows what happens when a
  vehicle leads the robot and how large the effect is, not how often a
  warehouse puts the robot in that situation.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.}\quad \flag{The per-axis split is a poor second witness and is not quoted as
one: a step of about \SI{90}{\degree} decomposes into Euler angles according
to the axis it falls on, so pitch holds \SIrange{12.74}{17.02}{\degree} in
every run while yaw and roll range from \SI{1.93}{} to \SI{26.16}{\degree}.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{10.}\quad VINS-Fusion carries a
smaller signature of the same kind: over its four runs the median of the
per-run pitch and roll RMS is \SI{1.05}{} and \SI{1.33}{\degree} against
\SI{0.24}{\degree} in yaw; \flag{whether that is a residual gravity error or the rigid fit absorbing a
tilt has not been separated, and it is reported as an observation.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{11.}\quad Both of the latter do turn, but at \SI{24.98}{} and
\SI{20.90}{\second}, five to nine seconds after the last refinement is
available, because the dedicated scale-and-gravity refinement the method
offers as the remedy for this case is reached only on the monocular path in
the implementation used here; on the stereo-inertial path the gravity
direction receives no further estimate after the second bundle adjustment. \flag{Excitation is confounded with layout: the two recordings with yaw in the
window are the U-shape worlds and the two without are the I-shape worlds, so
these are two routes against two routes and not sixteen independent samples.
The comparison that would separate them is a recording on the I layout whose
opening manoeuvre turns inside the first fifteen seconds, which does not yet
exist.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{12.}\quad \flag{The panel shows that timing and
  nothing more: on the four recordings that exist, yaw inside the window is a
  property of the layout, so this coincides with the gravity error rather than
  being shown to cause it.} (b) the published map rotation at the first
  refinement, which keeps the prior on the IMU biases, against the second,
  which drops it, paired within each of the sixteen runs; colours as in (a).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{13.}\quad \flag{The same regression on the closure-free runs of
\repo{realistic_001}, whose pitch and roll error is comparable at \SI{2.77}{}
and \SI{3.71}{\degree}, gives $r = \num{-0.49}$ and \num{-0.50} and a vertical
error of only \SIrange{0.28}{0.33}{\metre}. A tilt therefore does not convert
into drift at a rate that holds across routes, and the two must not be
pooled.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.}\quad The two families occupy opposite
  corners --- ORB-SLAM3 holds four times the memory for less than half the
  processor time --- and ORB-SLAM3's two front ends sit together on both
  axes, so the extractor is not what separates the pipelines here. \flag{Three repeats per configuration on one laptop, and the runs were not
  interleaved, so the bars measure repeatability inside a session and not the
  thermal state between sessions.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{15.\ \flag{[Confound: run order]}}\quad The six GPU runs were made consecutively
from 21:04 to 22:04 and the six CPU runs from 23:27 to 00:18, so the
I-recording GPU repeats were the fourth to sixth GPU runs of a session on a
laptop that throttles at \SI{90}{\celsius}; the front-end record notes that
timing comparisons need a cool-start, interleaved order. The six VINS-Fusion
runs are a separate session of 7 November and are not a control for that
state. The U-recording figures are the ones to quote until the I recording is
repeated interleaved.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{16.\ \flag{[Resolved: \repo{realistic_002/loopclosing_gpu}]}}\quad Earlier on 6 November this run was reported as closure-free from its
\repo{loop_closing.csv} and queried. Its manifest shows the real cause: it was
launched on the \repo{realistic_003} bag with \repo{realistic_002}'s output
path, so it was scored against the wrong truth (\SI{4.94}{\metre},
\SI{48.9}{\degree}, 139\,\% of the recording's frames processed). It is set
aside, not deleted; the configuration was re-run on the right bag the same
evening and every table here carries that run.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{17.\ \flag{[Open: the false closure is diagnosed, not fixed]}}\quad The \SI{14}{\metre} correction and the \SI{17.7}{\metre} separation of the
joined keyframes identify the \repo{realistic_001} closure as false, both
front ends agree, and the matched pair has now been inspected
(\reportref{fig:exp1-false-closure}): the same repeated asset from opposite sides
of the building. The two guards that would catch it (a covisibility-consistency
window, or a maximum correction against the inertial drift bound) are
untested. Until one is, the finding is a diagnosis, not a fix.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{18.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Four real recordings with an independent planar reference
(\repo{dataset_realv6_000}, \repo{dataset_realv7_000} to \repo{_002}). A
non-visual baseline exists: wheel+gyro dead reckoning with the feedback speed
scaled by a factor fitted once against the tracker on \repo{realv7_000} and
held on the other three. The visual arm is ORB-SLAM3 in four configurations on
each recording, sixteen runs, all made with the fork's patch-15
initialisation switches and scored with no repair applied; they give
\SIrange{0.404}{0.480}{\metre} on \repo{realv6_000},
\SIrange{0.255}{0.267}{} on \repo{realv7_000}, \SIrange{0.434}{0.445}{} on
\repo{_001} and \SIrange{0.192}{0.211}{} on \repo{_002}. Across the held
recordings the baseline and ORB-SLAM3 are in the same accuracy class, the
baseline leading on one, tying on one and losing the third. The EKF of the simulation
slot cannot be formed, because the rig publishes no steering measurement;
VINS-Fusion completes all three \repo{realv7} recordings once the fisheye
field of view is masked at \SI{70}{\degree} and the stereo extrinsic frozen,
at \SIrange{0.374}{0.676}{\metre}, behind both other families. Latency and
resources are measured on every reported run and repeated three times per
configuration on \repo{realv6_000}. The two domains are also compared as
inputs: the real recordings carry more image gradient and more corners per
megapixel than the simulated ones and starve neither estimator, and the
\numrange{4}{11} times worse per-metre drift is \num{1.9} times per second of
operation once the robot's \num{5.8} times longer inertial integration per
metre is accounted for. Every accuracy value is provisional until
the marker-to-IMU lever arm is measured.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{19.\ \flag{[Open: the realv6 scale]}}\quad On \repo{realv6_000} the path-length ratio gives $k=0.43$ where the three
\repo{realv7} bags give $0.32$ to $0.33$, yet the held $k=0.325$ scores a path
ratio of 1.04 on the matched samples. The export is at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} and
fails the validity rules, and the recording predates \repo{realv7} by three
days; whether the firmware unit changed or the sparse export misstates the
path length is not decided, and the \repo{realv6} row is a diagnostic.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{20.}\quad \flag{VINS-Fusion's failure on this recording was read as a delivery defect;
that reading is withdrawn. The root cause is the fisheye field of view
described under the \repo{realv7} results below. The counters below are kept
because they are what the defect looked like from the outside.} The node received 3\,187 of 6\,601
frames but used 6\,498 of the 43\,494 IMU messages it received, reset 217 times
on \repo{imu_gap}, and stopped after \SI{19}{\second}; behind that defect the
configuration still fixes a gravity norm of \num{9.2642} against the
\SI{9.878}{\metre\per\second\squared} this IMU reads at rest.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{21.}\quad \flag{One run per
configuration per recording, and the marker-to-IMU lever arm is unmeasured.
With the time offset settled, every estimator on every \repo{realv7} run
sits \SIrange{0.2}{0.4}{\metre} ahead of the tracker marker along the
direction of travel, and the wheel+gyro baseline, aligned with the identical
offset, does not: the scorer's diagnostic lever-arm fit reads \SI{0.31}{},
\SI{0.40}{} and \SI{0.23}{\metre} on the three recordings, consistent to
\SI{0.02}{\metre} within each, and would take the ORB-SLAM3 figures to
\SIrange{0.12}{0.21}{\metre}. That fit is not used; measuring the arm on
the rig is the single largest remaining correction to every real-rig
accuracy figure.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{22.}\quad \flag{Measured on the recordings, that
\SI{9.5}{\percent} is black: mean intensity \num{6.5} against
\numrange{103}{120} elsewhere, because it lies outside the lens image circle,
and no corner is ever detected in it. The polynomial's failure is therefore real
but inert, and what the mask actually discards is the
\SI{26}{\percent} of the corners an ORB detector finds in the image, those
between \SI{70}{\degree} and the edge of the image circle, which do carry
image. The divide-by-depth growth is the
operative mechanism; the non-monotonic polynomial is a calibration defect to fix,
not the cause of the divergence.} Second,
\texttt{estimate\_extrinsic} was left at 1, which lets the optimiser refine
the stereo baseline online and, on this rig, consume it; setting it to 0 holds
the calibrated baseline fixed.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{23.}\quad \flag{Two earlier explanations are withdrawn.} A previous revision attributed
the failure to delivery and configuration --- a stale gravity norm of
\num{9.2642} against the \SI{9.886}{\metre\per\second\squared} this IMU
reads at rest, and \SIrange{40}{45}{\percent} frame reception.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{24.}\quad \flag{Why VINS-Fusion's resident set is
\num{2.3} times its simulation value is not established; in-process JPEG
decoding of the compressed real recordings is a candidate, not a finding.} ORB-SLAM3's repeats agree to within \SI{4}{\percent} on back-end latency, CPU
and memory.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{25.}\quad \flag{On the same \repo{realv6} repeats, scored as diagnostics,
the closure-free configurations repeat their ATE to
\SIrange{0.02}{0.03}{\metre}, while one of the six loop-closing runs accepted a
single closure with a \SI{36.4}{\metre} correction and finished at
\SI{10.7}{\metre}: the loop closer decides on the robot as it does on the I
layout in simulation, and no loop-closing figure on the robot is safe from it.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{26.}\quad \flag{One run per cell. What the figure
  supports is the pattern across the six pairs, not any single line.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{27.\ \flag{[Sparse reference]}}\quad The tracker ran at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} rather than its nominal \SI{7}{\hertz} on
\repo{realv6}, and
the validity rules were written for the faster export. Either the export has to
be re-captured at full rate or a rule for sparse references has to be written
before any value from this recording is quoted outside a diagnostic.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{28.}\quad \flag{Sampled frames, twelve per recording, so the image statistics
  are indicative of the recording and not of every frame in it.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{29.}\quad \flag{One thing does get worse: ORB-SLAM3 converts
\SI{17.6}{\percent} of its extracted features into tracked map points on the
rig against \SI{31.3}{\percent} in simulation. Twice the supply, half the
conversion --- a matching and triangulation question, not a detection one, and
one this report does not answer.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{30.}\quad \flag{The real-rig ATE carries the
unmeasured lever arm and should not be read on its own; the relative-pose rows
are immune to it, since a constant offset cancels in a displacement.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{31.}\quad \flag{One run per
  configuration per recording on the real side; the comparison is between the
  medians of two populations and not a paired test, so it supports the size of
  the difference and not a per-configuration one.}

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Visual-Inertial Odometry on a Prior Map: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{32.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Five databases are scored for geometry and drivability:
the tiny warehouse, which passes, and four realistic-warehouse maps --- two
mapping recordings, one per layout, each built closure-free under two
back-end configurations, A and B --- all of which fail the quality
criterion fixed before scoring. The tiny map's independent drivability
reference remains lost.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{33.\ \flag{[Queried: reproducibility of the drivability half]}}\quad The geometry result is fully reproducible: both \repo{map/map_tiny.db} and the
world file are present. The drivability result is not. Its reference run,
\repo{dataset_static_tiny_repeat}, is absent from \repo{dataset/} and from the
removable drive, and the only surviving recording of this warehouse is the one
that built the map, which would answer a weaker question
(\reportref{sec:map-drivability}). The database additionally stores an empty parameter
set, so the configuration that produced it is not recoverable from the file, and
the RTAB-Map engineering record's claim that the node stamps match no dataset is
contradicted by the pose agreement reported above. The drivability figures should
therefore be read as a dated measurement rather than a standing result, and should
not be carried into the major report until an independent route has been recorded
and retained.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{34.}\quad The failure was attributed there to the front end under repeated
structure, not to the mapping back end. \flag{No database, run directory or figure for this attempt is registered in
the repository at the cutoff, so the result is reported on the strength of the
progress record and cannot be audited. A database identified from its contents
as this attempt (18 nodes, \SI{37}{\metre} along one aisle, poses leaving the
floor, placeable in no large world) was found among the unregistered
databases on 22 October 2026 and deleted with them on 6 November, unscored.
The attempt must be repeated with its artifacts retained before it is carried
into any conclusion.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{35.\ \flag{[Queried: front end of the realistic builds]}}\quad RTAB-Map took its pose from TF, so the odometry came from whichever front end
was running; none of the four databases records which, and the build Bs
were made during the latency sessions of Experiment~1, whose load on the front
end is not recorded either. The precision loss cannot be placed on the front
end against the back end, nor the November drop on parameters against session,
until the build manifest names both.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{36.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Six live runs of 15 November 2026, in the two static
worlds, measure the localisation against ground truth over hand-driven routes
of \SIrange{21}{148}{\metre}. Neither traffic world is measured, so
nothing here speaks to a dynamic warehouse. No goal was commanded in any of the
six either, so the goal-reaching measures of the reporting rules below are
still unused and that half of the experiment remains \status{planned}. The protocol, goal set and
success criteria are now fixed in code (\repo{script/exp4_protocol.yaml},
generated by \repo{script/exp4_goals.py}), which is what the previous revision
of this document recorded as missing. Mechanisms are analysed separately in
\path{insights/experiment_4_insight/}.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{37.}\quad The ground truth
reports the model origin and every estimate reports the camera/IMU body, so the
\SI{0.338}{\metre} lever arm is applied to the ground truth before the fit and
before any comparison, and never to recorded data. \flag{Two corrections belong on the record here.} First, an earlier revision
fitted the transform against uncorrected ground truth and reported the resulting
\SI{0.337}{\metre} residual as confirmation that the fit was right, on the
grounds that it equalled the lever arm.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{38.}\quad \paragraph{Reporting rules, goal-reaching.} \flag{Fixed before any run exists,
so that the result cannot be chosen after the fact, and left unchanged here.} A
goal counts as reached when the base frame is within \SI{1.0}{\metre} and
\SI{30}{\degree} of it and the planner reports success
(\texttt{goal\_tolerance\_m} and \texttt{goal\_tolerance\_deg} in
\repo{script/exp4_protocol.yaml}).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{39.}\quad \flag{A previous revision of this
paragraph quoted \SI{0.25}{\metre} and \SI{10}{\degree} as the goal
tolerance and a \SI{30}{\second} recovery limit. Neither matches the protocol
file this paragraph claims to be reporting: its tolerances are \SI{1.0}{\metre}
and \SI{30}{\degree}, which is also what \repo{script/exp4_score.py} prints,
and it encodes no recovery limit at all. The protocol itself has not been
edited since it was committed on 12 November; the error was in this prose, and
in the stricter direction, so the rules in force are looser than the slot
claimed. No goal-reaching result has been scored yet, so nothing reported
depended on it.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{40.}\quad \paragraph{Reporting rules, pose tracking.} \flag{Defined after these data
existed, and reported as the weaker claim it is.} Error is the planar distance
between the published \texttt{map}~$\rightarrow$~\texttt{base\_link} transform,
sampled at \SI{2}{\hertz}, and the lever-arm-corrected ground truth
interpolated to the same instants.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{41.}\quad \flag{Which runs these are, and which were retired.} The slot reports one
configuration throughout: \repo{correction_gate.py} enabled with a position
threshold of \SI{1.5}{\metre}, recorded on 15 November 2026.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{42.}\quad Both
are retired to \path{trash/} rather than reported beside their replacement. \flag{The \texttt{rep} index in the recording directories is a configuration
index and not a repeat index, so none of these runs are replicates of one
another and nothing here measures run-to-run spread.} The gate threshold is
printed as its own column by \repo{script/exp4_score.py} so that two tunings
cannot sit in one table looking alike.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{43.}\quad \flag{Two recordings were lost rather than retired.} A run in the U traffic
world, and later the three U-layout runs of the ungated configuration, were
overwritten on 15 November and their ground truth is unrecoverable.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{44.}\quad \flag{Splitting the panels exposes a pattern the single axis hid.} All six
  runs begin within \SIrange{0.108}{0.137}{\metre} of truth, but every
  I-layout run then climbs to five to eleven times that before a fix pulls it
  back --- \SI{0.519}{}, \SI{0.765}{} and \SI{1.229}{\metre}, each peaking
  between \SI{19.5}{} and \SI{23.0}{\metre} driven --- where no U-layout run
  exceeds twice its starting error.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{45.}\quad \flag{That bias is not uniform, which matters for what can be concluded from
it.} Only the I-layout straight is genuinely one-signed, with every sample
negative; the figure-of-eight is negative in \SI{75}{\percent} of its samples
and the square in \SI{56}{\percent}, crossing zero repeatedly.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{46.}\quad \flag{The previous revision drew a stronger conclusion from the same data ---
that the offset was route-dependent, \SIrange{0.32}{0.59}{\metre} on a single
aisle against \SIrange{0.02}{0.14}{\metre} over the building, and matched
Part~A's half-metre wall displacement. That pattern was the frame error,
which is larger on a straight run where the heading barely changes. It does not
survive the correction and is withdrawn.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{47.}\quad \flag{This is the clearest effect of the configuration, and the one claim the
slot can make about it.} An earlier configuration, reported in a previous
revision and now retired, put two runs over a metre for \SI{36}{} and
\SI{23.5}{\second} and as far as \SI{6.80}{\metre}, with the published pose
cutting diagonally through three shelf rows.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{48.}\quad Its correction neither
translates nor turns across the stretch --- yaw and $x$ hold at
\SI{-3.40}{\degree} and \SI{-10.17}{\metre} throughout --- which is what a
\emph{refused} correction looks like rather than a wrong one: the gate declined
to move the pose and it coasted on odometry until a fix was accepted again. \flag{A previous revision distinguished two excursion mechanisms, one
rotational and one translational, from two events in the retired
configuration. Those recordings no longer exist and the distinction is
withdrawn; one event cannot re-establish it.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{49.}\quad \flag{It does not follow
that the word count is uninformative, and an earlier revision of this paragraph
overstated it.} Among the rejections the zero-support and some-support groups
do differ in word count --- medians of \num{56} and \num{106} --- but their
ranges overlap across \numrange{24}{165}, and the rank correlation of
\num{0.24} is measured only where the inlier count is already truncated to
\numrange{0}{19} of the \num{20} needed, which attenuates it by construction.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{50.}\quad \flag{This is a replay of logged corrections, not a run with the gate switched
off.} The ungated configuration's own recordings were lost (above), and a robot
steered by Nav2 on a wrong pose would have driven differently; these routes were
hand-driven, so the path is the same either way.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{51.}\quad Planar error rises with the ground-truth yaw rate
in all six runs ($\rho$ \numrange{0.09}{0.76}, sign test $p = \num{0.031}$). \flag{It cannot be attributed to turning.} Yaw rate and speed are confounded in
every run ($\rho$ \numrange{0.34}{0.91}), so the measurement cannot separate
turning from simply moving, and part of the effect is the timebase recorded
below.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{52.}\quad \flag{Some of the reported error is timebase, and the slot cannot say how
much.} Fitting a constant time offset between each estimate and the ground
truth returns offsets of \emph{opposite sign}: the published pose matches best
when shifted \SIrange{-0.04}{-0.12}{\second}, the front end's own trajectory
when shifted \SIrange{+0.20}{+0.26}{\second}, on the same runs against the same
truth.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{53.}\quad \paragraph{Insight: over these distances the prior supplies a datum, not
accuracy.} \flag{This narrows the objective stated above, and is the claim the
data support.} Unaided ORB-SLAM3, rigidly aligned onto ground truth, drifts by a
median of \SIrange{0.013}{0.307}{\metre} over these \SIrange{21}{148}{\metre}
routes, never exceeds \SI{0.64}{\metre} at any instant, and ends each run
between \SI{0.02}{\metre} and \SI{0.42}{\metre} from truth.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{54.}\quad \flag{The ordering is suggestive and is not a measurement.} Six runs, one per
cell, on hand-driven routes that differ in shape as well as length, so route
length is confounded with layout and with everything else that differs between
cells; and a previous configuration of this same slot produced the opposite
split.

\medskip

reference geometry of the site exists to score one against, and so no
relocalization on the real robot can be scored either.}
